prerequisites: Adequate knowledge of fundamental methodological aspects of basic sciences (mathematical analysis, geometry, physics).
Knowledge of matrix algebra in the real and complex domain, derivatives, integrals, ordinary differential equations, Fourier series, Laplace transforms, fundamental laws of electromagnetism.
Ability to solve systems of algebraic equations in real and complex algebra, derive and integrate functions, solve systems of differential equations, apply Laplace transforms and anti-transforms.
Ability to formulate relationships between electrical quantities in resistors, capacitors, and inductors.
Recommended to have passed Mathematical Analysis 2, Applied Mathematics, Physics 2.
Prerequisite exams from the Course of Study: Mathematical Analysis 1 and Physics 1.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge and understanding of the constitutive relationships of lumped-parameter components, of the fundamental relationships of circuit theory, of theorems and methods for the analysis of steady-state circuits, of the symbolic method, of theorems and methods for the analysis of circuits in sinusoidal regime, of the state variable approach for the analysis of the dynamical behavior of a circuit, the use of the Laplace transform for circuit analysis, the frequency analysis of a circuit.

Apply knowledge and understanding to analyze a circuit with concentrated parameters in steady, sinusoidal and periodic conditions; derive the complete response of a circuit in the time domain and in the domain of the Laplace variable.
Demonstrate a professional approach to the modeling of an electromagnetic device using lumped parameter circuit representation and the analysis of simple passive and active filters.
Evaluate the applicability of theorems and methods for the analysis of lumped-parameter circuits to the analysis of electrical devices both in steady state and in dynamical behavior.
Construct the relative lumped parameter model for devices of medium complexity and solve the related model with the tools of circuit theory.
Perform frequency analysis of circuits and recognize the type of a passive and active filter.
Develop autonomy of judgment to clearly express technical concepts inherent in the study of electrical circuits and solve circuit problems never solved before.
Develop the ability to critically evaluate the results of circuit analysis.
Communicate the notions and methods learned, formalize problems in terms of circuit models with concentrated parameters and discuss related solutions to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors.

Integrate knowledge acquired from other courses (Mathematics and Physics, Systems Analysis and Measurements) and various sources to achieve a broad vision of problems related to electrical circuit analysis.
Develop the necessary skills to face subsequent courses with a high degree of autonomy.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of circuit theory: Voltage and current, Kirchhoff's first and second laws, Components and gates, Descriptive variables, Power and energy, Conventions.
General properties of components and circuits, basis of definition.
Resistor, Capacitor, Inductor, Independent Voltage and Current Generators, Controlled Generators, Operational Amplifier, Mutually Coupled Inductors, Ideal Transformer. Real components.
Steady-state circuit analysis: Components in series and in parallel. Star-triangle transformation; Topological notions.
Methods of analysis: meshes and knots.
Tellegen's theorem and principle of superposition of effects.
Thevenin's and Norton's theorems. Maximum power transfer theorem.
Analysis of circuits in sinusoidal regime: Presence of the time variable in the analysis of linear and permanent circuits. Sinusoidal and phasor functions.
Properties of phasors and phasor of derivative. The circuit transformed into the domain of the phasors.
Impedance and admittance. Phasors' method. Analysis of networks in sinusoidal regime. Theorems.

Power and energy in sinusoidal steady state, Complex power, Passive bipoles, Conservation of complex power (Boucherot), Theorem of maximum active power transfer, Superposition of powers, The problem of power factor correction.
Analysis of dual-port networks: Impedance matrix. Admittance matrix. Hybrid parameters. Thevenin and Norton's theorems on two-port networks.
Frequency response: Resonant circuits. Passive filters. Active filters.
Analysis of circuits in dynamic operation: Time domain analysis, input/output relationship and equations of state.
First-order and second-order examples. Main imprinted signals: unit impulse, unit step, sine wave.
Analysis in the domain of the Laplace variable: references to Laplace transforms, transformation of component equations and topological equations.
Network functions: circuit excitation and response, impulse response, properties of network functions. Stability.

assessment_methods.method: 2 intermediate partial tests (written form) for attending students
Written and oral exam during exam sessions for all students

assessment_rules: The final grade is expressed in thirtieths, weighing the grade attributed to the different exercises based on effort required in terms of content and computational complexity. A minimum evaluation of 18/30 is conferred when knowledge/skills are at least elementary. An evaluation of 30/30 with possible honors is given when knowledge is excellent. The mid-term tests are exhaustive for the assessment of learning outcomes for attending students. Students who did not participate, did not achieve positive results, or want to renounce intermediate results must take the full written and oral exam.
